acceptedAnswer.text: Divide mass by volume. A block of 1,962.5 g with a volume of 250 cm³ has a density of 7.85 g/cm³.
The ratio of a material's density to the density of water. Water is 1, steel is about 7.85, and anything below 1 floats in water.

mainEntity.name: How do I convert g/cm³ to kg/m³?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiply by 1,000. Steel at 7.85 g/cm³ is 7,850 kg/m³.

mainEntity.name: Why does the fill percentage matter?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 3D print or foam is not solid material. A part at 20% infill has roughly one fifth of the solid material's density plus its outer walls, so treat this as an estimate.
Yes. Most materials expand when heated and become less dense. The change is small for solids and larger for liquids and gases.
